title: Append one root factor to two supplied normalized morphisms
statement: For a Noetherian scheme T, prime ell, and n,d, suppose f in tensor degree d+1 and g in tensor degree 1 are supplied and each is GeneratorCompatible. Then there is a GeneratorCompatible morphism in degree d+2. No invertibility of ell is assumed. This is an inductive tensor operation on two actual morphisms, not existence in every degree.

source.place: Step 2: Existence of the normalized integral Tate quotient morphism

proof.text: Use the positive-degree finite-twist recursion and the normalized tensor constraint of the comparison pullback.
Transport its tensor through scalar realization using the constant-scalar tensor comparison, then apply f tensor g.

Use the inverse extension-of-scalars tensor constraint and contract the extra unit in integralLine 1. Split root tuples into castSucc and last, put a in the first factor and 1 in the last, and apply the two given compatibility equations. The resulting pure tensor is the defining integralGenerator recursion.

proof_origin.place: Step 2: degree-zero multiplication, first root projection, and tensor induction

lean.statement:
theorem tateTensorQuotient_generator_step
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T] (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (n d : ℕ)
    (f : (realization T ell n).obj (finiteSheaf T ell n (d + 1)) ⟶
      quotientLine T ell n (d + 1))
    (g : (realization T ell n).obj (finiteSheaf T ell n 1) ⟶ quotientLine T ell n 1)
    (hf : GeneratorCompatible T ell n (d + 1) f)
    (hg : GeneratorCompatible T ell n 1 g) :
    ∃ h : (realization T ell n).obj (finiteSheaf T ell n (d + 2)) ⟶
      quotientLine T ell n (d + 2),
      GeneratorCompatible T ell n (d + 2) h
